item.title: AI griefbots could change how we mourn — but there are serious risks ahead
item.description: A researcher from the University of Essex dives into the philosophical and ethical questions surrounding "deathbots."

item.title: 'Runaway' black hole detected by the James Webb telescope adds a strange new chapter to our universe's story
item.description: Recent observations suggest that 'runaway' black holes are tumbling through the cosmos. Building on decades of theory, the discovery adds a remarkable new chapter to the story of the universe.

item.title: In a first, study links maternal genes to risk of pregnancy loss
item.description: For the first time, scientists have identified genetic variants that increase the risk of aneuploidy, in which cells have an abnormal number of chromosomes. Aneuploidy in egg cells can lead to miscarriage.

item.title: Ancient rock art depicting hunters and geometric shapes discovered in Egypt's Sinai Desert — and it spans a period of 10,000 years
item.description: A rock shelter with rock art and inscriptions spanning millennia has been discovered in Egypt.

item.title: How long do most planets last?
item.description: Planets are born, and they can also "die." So what's the lifespan of a typical planet?

item.title: Deepest views from James Webb and Chandra telescopes reveal a monster object that defies theory — Space photo of the week
item.description: The James Webb Space Telescope and the Chandra X-ray Observatory have captured the clearest image yet of a galaxy cluster in the making, seen when the universe was only one billion years old.

item.title: Lucky few to see 'ring of fire' solar eclipse over Antarctica on Feb. 17
item.description: This month's new moon brings an annular (or "ring of fire") solar eclipse, but it will only be visible from parts of Antarctica.

item.title: 'The brain consistently moved upward and backward': Astronauts' brains physically shift in their heads during spaceflight
item.description: A new study analyzed brain MRI scans from 26 astronauts and found that the longer someone lived in space, the more their brain shifted in their skull.

item.title: Snakes keep evolving into cannibals — here's what scientists think is going on
item.description: A review of over 500 reports of cannibalistic behavior in snakes finds it's appeared multiple times in different evolutionary lineages, leading researchers to hypothesize it's beneficial for snakes under certain circumstances.

item.title: Vaccine denial sets Americans up for more chronic illness
item.description: Despite well-established links between pathogens and chronic illness, the U.S. government continues to weaken public health measures to treat and prevent infectious diseases — a strategy that will ultimately make Americans even sicker.
